sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 closed Monday at 7,417, about 4.4% below its 1-month high and near the bottom of that range, down 3.6% over the month. The Nasdaq 100 is weaker still at 27,197, down 7.9% over the month and 8.8% off its high. The VIX sits at 22.9, up from 20.0 a month ago and below its 1-month high of 28.2. The Euro Stoxx 50 is the contrast: up 2.3% over the month and within 1% of its high. The week brings 15 scheduled reports from the tracked universe, concentrated in technology (6) and consumer names (5).

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: All 15 dates are cadence-model estimates, not confirmed. Monday (Nov 23): HPE and ZM report into the technology group, median +0.25% off recent prints. Tuesday (Nov 24) is the heaviest day: HPQ, ADI, NTNX and WDAY in technology, BBY, BURL and DKS in consumer-cyclical (median +0.47%), and DLTR and SJM in consumer-defensive (median -0.28%). MDT reports the same day in healthcare (median -0.09%). Wednesday (Nov 25): DE reports into industrials (median +0.39%).

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Copper (-2.53% median, 6 tickers, 230 news items) and mining (-2.53%, 215 tickers, 2,765 news items) lead the reaction table, both negative. Energy is the largest positive at +1.94% across 315 tickers and 5,115 news items. Mining and energy have thick news windows; copper's is thin. None of this week's reporters sit in these three groups, so these reads are backdrop rather than direct earnings setups.
